selected.title: Webb spotted a starry ring galaxy from the universe’s early days
selected.summary: Astronomers identified GS18660, a ring-shaped galaxy observed as it was billions of years younger than the universe is today. Researchers say a head-on collision may have created its unusual shape.
selected.why_it_matters: A rare shape in the distant past offers clues to how galaxies collide, form stars, and change over cosmic time.
selected.challenge_question: What may have given the distant galaxy GS18660 its ring shape?
selected.answer_explanation: The researchers describe GS18660 as a ring galaxy possibly formed by a head-on collision; that explanation is supported, not proven.
selected.butterfly_question: How do galaxy collisions turn cosmic wreckage into new stars and structures?
